heroHeadline: Viv Ansanm Destroys Marchand-Dessalines Police Station; PM Departs for Vatican; Moïse Assassination Trial Jury Deliberating
heroSubtitle: On May 7, 2026, Viv Ansanm gang forces destroyed the police station in Marchand-Dessalines — a strategic Artibonite town on Route Nationale 1 approximately 109 km north of Port-au-Prince — prompting Haitian security forces to launch anti-terrorist 'Operation Viv Ansanm' in which more than 10 gang members were killed, marking a sharp escalation of Artibonite instability following Gran Grif's March–April 2026 offensive that killed 16–70 people in Jean-Denis and displaced 13,000+. On May 8, Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé departed for an official diplomatic mission to Rome and the Vatican (May 8–11) to consolidate international support and humanitarian cooperation, drawing criticism from Haitian-language media who noted 'gangs are gaining ground while Fils-Aimé collects foreign trips' as Saint-Marc (Artibonite) entered its third day under nightly curfew. In Miami, the jury in the federal Moïse assassination trial was in its third day of deliberations (started May 6) following closing arguments on May 4–5, with four defendants (Arcangel Pretel Ortiz, Antonio Intriago, Walter Veintemilla, James Solages) awaiting verdict — the first major judicial reckoning for the July 7, 2021 assassination that triggered Haiti's cascading governance collapse. Earlier in the week: the Dominican Republic formally committed $20 million to the UN Gang Suppression Force Trust Fund (May 5, two-year tranche); Haiti's Provisional Electoral Council set a 30,000-member party registration threshold for August 2026 elections (May 6); the UN International Migration Review Forum in New York hosted Foreign Minister Raina Forbin (May 5); and the US Coast Guard transferred 1.4 tons of intercepted marijuana to the Haitian National Police (May 5). Gang control of Port-au-Prince remains contested between PM Fils-Aimé's claimed ~75% (May 1 CNN/Amanpour interview) and UN BINUH's March 2026 independent estimate of approximately 90%. A US Supreme Court ruling on TPS (Noem v. Doe / Trump v. Miot) affecting approximately 350,000 Haitian TPS holders remains pending after April 29 oral arguments; a decision is expected by late June or early July 2026.
